Where is Richland County and what is in it?

Richland County is in the Midlands of South Carolina, and its seat is Columbia, which is also the state capital and the largest community. The county covers 771.96 square miles, with 757.28 of land and 14.68 of water.

Besides Columbia, the municipalities are Cayce, Forest Acres, Arcadia Lakes, Blythewood, Eastover, Elgin and Irmo.

  • Fairfield and Newberry counties lie to the north and northwest.
  • Kershaw and Sumter counties are to the northeast and east.
  • Lexington County is to the west and Calhoun County to the south.

The county's 2020 Census population was 416,147.

What is the history of Richland County?

Richland County was established on March 12, 1785, and is probably named for its rich land. It began as part of the Camden District, and its boundaries were formally incorporated on December 18, 1799.

Landmarks that define it today include the South Carolina State House in downtown Columbia, the University of South Carolina, Fort Jackson and the McEntire Joint National Guard Base. Riverbanks Zoo is reached by I-126.

Where do you pay Richland County property tax?

Richland County property tax is paid through the Treasurer at 2020 Hampton Street, Columbia, SC 29204, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The main number is 803-576-2250.

Taxes can be paid online, in person or by mail, and the county offers a monthly payment plan. The Treasurer's pages list separate emails for customer service (treasurer@richlandcountysc.gov), planned payments and tax sale questions.

  • State law makes January 15 the end of the penalty-free window (S.C. Code 12-45-70).
  • A 3% penalty follows, then 7% more before February 2 and 5% more before March 17 (S.C. Code 12-45-180).
  • A payment plan does not stop further action unless the full amount is paid.

Statute section 12-45-180 also waives penalties when title transferred during the tax year and the new owner never received a timely notice.

What does the Richland County tax sale look like?

Richland County's tax sale is typically held each fall and is run as a sealed bid auction, and the 2026 sale was set for November 2 and 3 at the Richland County Township Auditorium, 1703 Taylor Street, Columbia. Property is sold as is, for cash, to the highest bidder.

To stop a property from being sold, the Treasurer's office had to receive payment by 5 p.m. on Friday, October 30, 2026, in cash or certified cashier's check. Personal, company and escrow checks were not accepted.

  • Bidders register online only, and the fee is $50.00.
  • The opening bid is the delinquent taxes, sale costs and current year taxes.
  • A winning bidder who does not pay owes $500 per bid plus court costs.
  • Buyers receive title without warranty, and the county can cancel a sale before a deed is issued.

How often does Richland County reassess?

The Richland County Assessor conducts a countywide reassessment every five years, consistent with S.C. Code 12-43-217. The Assessor's page does not name the next year, so ask the office at 803-576-2640.

The state rule also says taxpayers must be notified when value or classification changes by $1,000 or more. A county can delay putting new values into effect by ordinance for no more than one tax year.

The Assessor's office also handles rollback taxes on farmland that changes use, HOA properties, active military residential exemptions and deed sale records. The office also lists multiple-lot and builder or developer discounts, commercial ATI exemptions and mailing address changes among its services, so tell it when you sell or move.

How do you appeal a Richland County assessment?

File a written objection with the Assessor within 90 days of the dated reassessment notice, or by the first penalty date on the tax bill if no notice was sent. For online appeals, the deadline is whichever comes first.

  1. File through the county's "Appeal Your Assessment" portal or in writing.
  2. Attach documents that dispute the assessed value or classification.
  3. If a representative files for you, submit a power of attorney on SC DOR Form SC2848.
  4. For an LLC or similar owner, include Articles of Organization or an Operating Agreement.

The Assessor is at 2020 Hampton Street, Suite 2058, Columbia, SC 29204, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 192, Columbia, SC 29202. The phone is 803-576-2640 and the email is assessoroffice@richlandcountysc.gov. The county site also lists a Board of Assessment Appeals that hears disputes between the Assessor and the taxpayer.

What does the 4% legal residence rate mean in Richland County?

Qualifying owner-occupied homes move from the 6% assessment ratio to 4% once residency and ownership requirements are met. State law covers the home plus up to five contiguous acres, and the owner may not rent it for more than 72 days in a calendar year (S.C. Code 12-43-220).

If an owner loses eligibility and fails to report it within six months, the statute allows a penalty of 100% of the tax paid plus interest of 0.5% per month, with a $30 minimum.

Landlords and heirs who do not live in the house should expect the 6% rate. Active-duty residents with South Carolina duty stations are treated as domiciled here under the same section.

  • Assessor, 803-576-2640: rate, value and appeals.
  • Deed recording: $1.85 per $500 of value, split $1.30 state and $0.55 county (S.C. Code 12-24-10), with deeds in lieu of foreclosure exempt.

Greenville County by the numbers

Where is Greenville County and how is it laid out?

Greenville County sits in the northwest corner of South Carolina's Upstate, against the North Carolina line. It covers 795.57 square miles, of which 785.93 are land, and the city of Greenville is both the county seat and its largest community.

The northern boundary follows the crest of the Blue Ridge Mountains, so the county reaches higher country than most of the state. The 2010 Census lists six cities: Fountain Inn, Greenville, Greer, Mauldin, Simpsonville and Travelers Rest. Fountain Inn and Greer each spill across a county line, into Laurens and Spartanburg counties.

Much of the population lives in places that are not cities at all. Taylors, Berea, Wade Hampton, Five Forks, Gantt and Slater-Marietta are census-designated places, and each has its own mix of older ranch homes, newer subdivisions and mill-era cottages.

For a seller this layout matters because a house in Travelers Rest near the mountains and a house in Mauldin near the interstate are taxed by the same county offices but sell to very different buyers.

What is the history behind Greenville County?

The state legislature created Greenville County in 1786, and the name honors General Nathanael Greene, the Revolutionary War commander of the southern campaign. The early spelling was "Greeneville."

The county grew out of the old Ninety-Six District as settlers moved into the backcountry. The census count was 6,503 in 1790 and 53,490 in 1900. By 1950 it had reached 168,152, and it has kept climbing since.

That long growth curve explains why a single county can hold homes from the 1900s, the mill villages, the postwar subdivisions and houses finished last year. Age is the first thing a cash buyer looks at when estimating repairs, and Greenville County has every age.

How big is Greenville County and what does its economy rely on?

Greenville County is the most populous county in South Carolina, with 525,534 residents in the 2020 Census and a 2025 estimate of 583,125. Its 2022 economic output was about $40.6 billion, and unemployment ran between 2.1 and 3.3 percent from 2022 to 2024.

Health care and social assistance is the largest industry by jobs, with 43,180 workers out of 292,366. Manufacturing follows with 31,693 jobs, then retail trade with 30,485.

  • Employers named for the county include Bon Secours, Charter Communications, GE Vernova, Lockheed Martin and Michelin.
  • Prisma Health, Publix, TD Bank, the Postal Service and Walmart appear on the same list.
  • These sectors are the county's biggest sources of paychecks.

The 2025 estimate shows the county still adding people.

What roads, airports and rail serve Greenville County?

Interstates 85, 185 and 385 are the main highways, with US 25, 29, 123 and 276 crossing the county as well. Many residents live along these corridors and drive to jobs elsewhere in the county.

Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport lies mostly in Spartanburg County, while Donaldson Center Airport and Greenville Downtown Airport are inside Greenville County. Amtrak serves the city at its Greenville station.

A cash buyer prices location in whatever it is, so you do not have to stage the house or wait for a buyer who likes the road.

When are Greenville County property taxes due, and what does a late bill cost?

Real property tax in Greenville County is due without penalty by January 15. Bills usually go out near the end of October, according to the county's Real Property Services calendar.

These dates match S.C. Code 12-45-180. The Tax Collector says penalties come off only when there is direct evidence of a county error.

The office is in the South Building, Suite 1100-S, and the phone is 864.467.7050. You can pay in person, by mail or online, and most payments post within three to five business days.

The county also states that the tax on a property follows the property, not the person. If you sell with the current year unpaid, the title company normally settles the balance from your proceeds.

How does selling a house change the assessment in Greenville County?

A sale is usually an assessable transfer of interest, which means the county revalues the house to a current date. Real Property Services says the 15 percent cap on increases is removed after such a transfer, and a point-of-sale reassessment uses a December 31 appraisal date for the year of the transfer.

Ownership on January 1 decides whose name is printed on the bill. If the deed changes after that date, both the old and new owners appear on that year's bill, and only the new owner appears the following year. A new assessment notice usually arrives the year after the change.

  • Owner-occupied homes get the 4 percent legal residence assessment, plus a credit that removes the school operating tax. The application must be hand-delivered or postmarked by January 15 with an original signature, and electronic filing is not accepted.
  • A buyer who will not live in the house loses that treatment, so the bill can rise sharply for the next owner.
  • The county lists a January 30 deadline for the 25 percent exemption on transfers made the previous year.

Telling your buyer about this ahead of time avoids a surprise after closing. A short call to Real Property Services at 864.467.7300 clears up anything unclear.

How do you appeal a Greenville County assessment?

You appeal in writing, and the first deadline is printed on your assessment notice. If no notice was sent, the usual deadline is January 15, or the next working day if that falls on a weekend or holiday.

The statute behind this is S.C. Code 12-60-2510, which gives 90 days from the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more.

  1. Mail a written objection with the tax map number, your reasons and your opinion of value. Email and fax are not accepted, and the postmark decides timeliness.
  2. A certified appraiser reviews every timely appeal, and the assessor mails the result.
  3. You have 30 days from the notice of decision to protest to the County Board of Assessment Appeals.
  4. You have 30 days after the Board's written decision to go to the Administrative Law Judge Division.

Appeals go to Real Property Services at Greenville County Square, Suite 1000. The office schedules notices for new construction and other increases in late summer or early fall.

What happens if Greenville County taxes go unpaid?

After March 17 the bill is delinquent and the Tax Collector issues an execution notice. If the bill is still unpaid 30 days after that notice is mailed, a Notice of Seizure follows by certified mail with restricted delivery.

The sale is a public auction at the Greenville Convention Center on Exposition Drive. The sale is advertised once a week for three weeks first, and the opening bid covers all delinquent tax, penalties and costs plus the current year's tax.

The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem within 12 months. Interest on the bid is 3 percent in months one to three, 6 percent in months four to six, 9 percent in months seven to nine and 12 percent in months ten to twelve. If nobody redeems, the buyer gets a tax deed that conveys only the county's interest, not a warranty deed.

Selling before the auction is often cleaner than letting the process run. A sale closes the debt through escrow, and you avoid the redemption interest.

What does it cost to record the deed in Greenville County?

Deeds are recorded at the Register of Deeds in Suite S-2100 of Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge, Monday to Friday from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm. The office asks you to arrive by 4:30 pm.

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value or part of it, according to S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 24. The statute splits that into $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. Some transfers are exempt, including a deed in lieu of foreclosure to the mortgagee and certain family partnership or trust transfers.

Your title or escrow company normally prepares the deed and pays the fee from closing funds. If you mail a deed yourself, include a cover letter with a phone number, a stamped return envelope and a check payable to Greenville County.

Can I sell my Greenville County house if the taxes are unpaid?

Yes. Unpaid tax follows the property, so it is paid from your sale proceeds at closing. A cash purchase can close with the balance cleared through escrow.

Who handles assessment appeals in Greenville County?

Real Property Services does, at Greenville County Square, Suite 1000, phone 864.467.7300. Objections must be in writing, and the postmark decides whether you met the deadline.

Does selling my home raise the next owner's tax bill?

Often it does. A sale is usually an assessable transfer of interest, which removes the 15 percent cap and sets a new value. The buyer also loses the 4 percent legal residence rate if the house is not their home.

How long do I have to redeem a house sold at a Greenville County tax sale?

You have 12 months from the sale. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem by paying the taxes, penalties, costs and the stepped interest on the bid.

Where is Lexington County and what does it include?

Lexington County is in the Midlands of South Carolina and is part of the Columbia metropolitan area. It covers 757.62 square miles, with 58.62 of those square miles being water, mostly because of Lake Murray.

The town of Lexington is the county seat and largest community, with 23,568 residents in 2020. West Columbia, Cayce, Irmo, Batesburg-Leesville, Chapin and Gaston are among the other municipalities, and large unincorporated places include Seven Oaks, Oak Grove, Red Bank and White Knoll. Parts of Columbia, Cayce, Irmo and Batesburg-Leesville cross county lines into Richland or Saluda counties.

A lake-area house, a subdivision near Irmo and a rural parcel near Gilbert are all in one county, but they sell on very different timelines.

Distribution centers cluster in the Saxe Gotha Industrial Park near Cayce. A mix of hospital, school and state jobs means sellers here are not tied to one employer, though a house with a leaking roof still needs repair or a buyer who will take it as is.

What roads, schools and weather should a Lexington County seller know about?

Three interstates touch Lexington County: I-20, I-26 and I-77, which begins in Cayce. Columbia Metropolitan Airport serves the area and the COMET authority provides public transit.

Five school districts cover parts of the county, and District 1 is the largest, with 27,072 students and 31 schools. Midlands Technical College and the county library system are also based here.

The climate is humid. Average rainfall is about 47 inches a year, with a July high near 92 degrees and a January low near 33 degrees. Wet summers are hard on roofs, gutters and crawl spaces, and a house on or near Lake Murray or the Saluda, Broad and Congaree rivers should be checked for drainage and flood questions before a buyer's inspector does it.

When are Lexington County property taxes due?

Lexington County real property notices are mailed to the owner of record after October 1, and full payment is due by January 15 of the next year. Payments postmarked after that date pick up penalties on January 16, February 2 and March 17.

The Treasurer's page does not give the percentages, but S.C. Code 12-45-180 sets them at 3 percent, then an added 7 percent, then an added 5 percent. Penalties keep accruing during a penalty appeal unless the full amount is paid, and the county refunds penalties already paid if the appeal is granted. The Treasurer takes written penalty appeals; call (803) 785-8217 for instructions.

The county also runs an installment program for real property that is not paid through escrow. Enrollees make five advance payments based on the prior year's tax, and the balance is billed by November 15. Enrollment renews each year, and opting out requires written consent, so a seller in the program should ask the Treasurer how to handle it before closing.

How do you appeal a Lexington County assessment?

A Lexington County owner files a written appeal with the Assessor within 90 days of the date on the assessment notice. If no notice arrived, the county's FAQ says the window is January 1 through January 15 of the following year.

The county reviews appeals on market value, and disagreeing with the dollar amount of the bill is not a ground. If the appeal is not resolved by December 31, the bill is based on at least 80 percent of the assessed value, and tax is still due January 15. After resolution, you either get a refund with interest or owe the difference with interest.

The county has a nine-member Board of Assessment Appeals appointed by County Council. It meets when requested in the Council Chambers of the County Administration Building, and its agendas are posted on the county meeting portal. The state notice rule applies as well: notices are required when value rises $1,000 or more, and the county page says the previous reassessments were in 2015 and 2020 on a five-year cycle, so ask the Assessor for the current schedule.

What changes when a Lexington County house is sold?

The seller's unpaid tax is settled from the proceeds at closing, and the buyer must apply for the 4 percent legal residence ratio. State law says that application must be filed before the first penalty date of the year the owner first claims it.

The county moves from an execution notice to a notice of seizure, then to a public auction. Newberry County is in central South Carolina and covers 647.28 square miles, of which 630.29 are land. It is bordered by Union, Fairfield, Lexington, Richland, Saluda, Greenwood and Laurens counties.

The city of Newberry is the county seat and largest community. Chappells, Stoney Hill, Jalapa and Kinards, which is partly in Laurens County, are other named communities. Newberry County was formed in 1785 from the Ninety-Six District, and the town of Newberry was founded in 1789 as its seat. The origin of the name is unknown, though one theory ties it to Quaker settlers and Newbury Park in London.

Cotton was the main crop before the Civil War. The railroad reached the county in the early 1850s, the Lutheran Church founded Newberry College in 1856, and the first cotton mills opened in the 1880s.

Where is Kershaw County, SC, and how is it laid out?

Kershaw County is in north-central South Carolina, part of the Columbia metropolitan area, with Camden as its county seat and largest community. It covers 740.26 square miles, of which 726.61 are land, and it touches Lancaster, Chesterfield, Darlington, Sumter, Lee, Richland and Fairfield counties.

What is the history behind Kershaw County?

Camden was settled around 1732 and is described as the oldest inland city in South Carolina. Kershaw County was created in 1791 and named for Col. Joseph Kershaw. From about 1800 to 1867 it was called Kershaw District.

The British held Camden from June 1780 to May 1781, and the Battle of Camden in August 1780 was a major American defeat. Union troops under Sherman burned parts of the town in February 1865. From the 1880s, northern families wintered in Camden, which built the horse culture that continues with the Carolina Cup steeplechase at Springdale Race Course. DuPont opened an Orlon plant in 1950 that was the largest employer for decades until production ended in 1990.

That history means older houses and old lots, and sometimes old deeds. Sellers who inherited a Camden home should expect the title search to go back through several owners.

What drives the Kershaw County economy?

Retail, health care and manufacturing lead local employment. In the third quarter of 2023 the county had 16,741 jobs at an average annual wage of $45,472. The largest sectors were retail trade at 3,653 jobs, health care and social assistance at 2,497, and manufacturing at 2,392.

Who handles property tax in Kershaw County?

Kershaw County splits property tax among three offices at the Kershaw County Government Center in Camden: the Assessor in Room 100, the Auditor in Room 120, and the Treasurer in Room 140. The Assessor values real property and mobile homes, measures new construction, takes value appeals and processes 4 percent legal residence and agricultural applications. The Auditor handles homestead exemptions. The Treasurer collects real and personal taxes and fees, and issues motor vehicle decals.

How do you appeal a Kershaw County assessment?

You object in writing to the Assessor within 90 days after the assessor mails the assessment notice. In a year with no notice, you may appeal in writing at any time; an appeal made before the first penalty date applies to that tax year.

  1. Request a conference. The Assessor must schedule it within 30 days of the request, or as soon as practical.
  2. File a written protest within 30 days after the conference.
  3. Expect a written response, generally within 30 days of the protest.
  4. Appeal to the county Board of Assessment Appeals within 30 days of that response.
  5. Ask for a contested case hearing in the Administrative Law Court within 30 days of the Board's written decision.

If the case is not resolved by December 31, the Assessor tells the auditor to adjust the bill to 80 percent of the protested amount, and any difference is settled with interest after the final decision. These steps come from Sections 12-60-2510 to 12-60-2550. What is the 4 percent legal residence rate in Kershaw County?

An owner-occupied home that is the owner's legal residence, with up to five contiguous acres, is taxed on 4 percent of its fair market value rather than 6 percent. You must apply on or before the first penalty date for the first year of the claim, and the home cannot be rented for more than 72 days in a calendar year.

A buyer of your house does not inherit your status; they must file their own. Section 12-43-220 also sets a penalty of 100 percent of the tax if someone holds the rate wrongly. Agricultural land can qualify at 4 percent in some cases, and a change of use brings rollback taxes for the current year and the three before it. The rules sit in Chapter 43 of Title 12.

State law also lets owners get a notice when value or classification changes by $1,000 or more.

What does a Kershaw County deed cost at closing?

The county seat and largest community is the city of Laurens. Clinton is the other main town, and the county also includes Cross Hill, Gray Court, Waterloo, Barksdale, Hickory Tavern, Madden and Owings. Fountain Inn is mostly in Greenville County, Ware Shoals is mostly in Greenwood County, and Kinards straddles the line with Newberry County.

The 2020 census counted 67,539 residents, and about 64 percent of the population lived in rural areas. For a seller, that rural share matters because a farmhouse outside Gray Court and a bungalow in the city of Laurens are taxed by the same county offices but attract very different buyers.

What shaped Laurens County, and what does it mean for older houses?

The county was formed on March 12, 1785, and was named for Henry Laurens, a president of the Continental Congress. It was one of nine modern counties carved from the old Ninety-Six District.

The Battle of Musgrove Mill, an American Revolution engagement, took place here. Andrew Johnson, later the 17th president, worked as a tailor in the town of Laurens in the 1820s. Presbyterian College in Clinton was founded in 1880.

How do you challenge an assessment in Laurens County?

A Laurens County owner objects in writing to the Assessor, and under state law the deadline is 90 days after the Assessor mails the assessment notice. The objection can cover fair market value, special use value or the assessment ratio.

State law requires a written notice only when the Assessor raises a value by $1,000 or more or assesses a property for the first time. South Carolina assesses a legal residence at 4 percent of fair market value and other real property at 6 percent. A house that fails the legal residence test is therefore assessed at one and a half times the ratio of an owner-occupied home.

Unpaid Laurens County taxes lead to a delinquent tax sale run by the Delinquent Tax Collector's office under Chapter 51 of Title 12 of the state code. The owner keeps the right to redeem the property for twelve months after the sale.

Oconee County was formed in 1868 when the state legislature divided Pickens County. The name comes from the Cherokee word Ae-quo-nee, usually given as "land beside the water."

What happens in an Oconee County tax sale, and can the owner get the house back?

A tax sale in Oconee County is an auction of the property to the highest bidder, and the owner has one year from the sale date to redeem. The sale is a collection method under S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 51.

The owner, a grantee from the owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem by paying the taxes, assessments, penalties and costs plus interest on the full bid. That interest rises by quarter.

Taxes do not disappear at closing. They are normally prorated between the parties, and any bill open in January should be paid from the proceeds so a new owner never inherits a penalty.

By January 15, with notices going out in the fall. The county expected online notices by October 10 and mailed notices by October 20 for 2026.

A 3% penalty applies after January 15, then another 7% before February 2 and another 5% before March 17. After March 17 the bill goes to collection.

You have 90 days from the date on the assessment notice to object in writing to the Assessor. If no notice was issued, the county allows an appeal until January 15 of the following year.

Yes, for one year from the sale date, by paying the taxes, costs and penalties plus interest of 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% depending on the quarter. After that the property is conveyed to the buyer.

The present county was created in 1800 from the western half of Charleston District and reorganized as a county in 1868. The county page we opened does not list payment methods, so call the Treasurer to confirm how you can pay.

What happens to delinquent real property taxes in Jasper County?

Delinquent real property in Jasper County can end up at a tax sale, and the owner then has 12 months to redeem. The county's real property collection page lays out this timeline under Section 12-51-40:

  • March 17: taxes become delinquent.
  • April 1: delinquent notices are mailed.
  • Usually September: certified notices go out for delinquent real estate and mobile homes.
  • Three consecutive Wednesdays before the sale: the county advertises the properties in a local paper.
  • First Monday of November: the sale takes place at the Clementa C. Pinckney Government Building, 358 Third Avenue, Ridgeland.

After the sale, the owner, a mortgage company or a grantee can pay the taxes and sale costs within 12 months from the sale date to take the property back. For a seller, that clock is a deadline for any plan to save the house or sell it. Selling before the first Monday of November lets the back taxes be paid out of the sale proceeds.

How do you appeal a Jasper County property assessment?

You appeal in writing, starting with the Assessor, and the first deadline is 90 days after the assessment notice was mailed. Jasper County lays out the steps on its Assessor Appeals page, and they follow Sections 12-60-2510 to 12-60-2550 of the state code.

  1. Ask the Assessor in writing for a meeting. The conference is set within about 30 days, and missing it waives further appeal for that year.
  2. If the issue is not settled, file a written protest within 30 days of the conference or the Assessor's Notice of Action. Include your name, address, phone, a description of the property, your reasons, and the value and classification you believe are correct.
  3. The Assessor responds in writing, usually within about 30 days.
  4. Appeal to the county Board of Assessment Appeals within 30 days of that response, or the new value becomes final.
  5. Exchange evidence at least 15 days before the Board conference, and file replies at least 7 days before.
  6. Request a contested case hearing at the Administrative Law Court within 30 days of the Board's written decision.

In years with no assessment notice, you can appeal at any time. An appeal filed before January 15 counts for that tax year, and one filed on or after January 15 counts for the next. Only authorized persons may act for an owner, such as an attorney, CPA, fiduciary or appraiser, and the authorization must name a specific individual.

If the appeal is not finished by December 31, state law has the assessor tell the auditor to bill at 80 percent of the protested amount, then true up later with interest.

Under South Carolina law, an owner-occupied legal residence and up to five contiguous acres are taxed on 4 percent of fair market value. Owners must apply on or before the first penalty date for the first year they claim it, and the home cannot be rented for more than 72 days in a calendar year.

Claiming the rate when you do not qualify carries a penalty of 100 percent of the tax paid plus interest. Jasper County also has a page for reporting residential exemption fraud. Values are revisited every fifth year, and owners must be told about any change of $1,000 or more. A county can postpone new values by one tax year by ordinance. Ask the Assessor which year Jasper County is on.

  • Schools named by the county include Hardeeville Elementary, Hardeeville Junior and Senior High, Ridgeland Elementary and Ridgeland Secondary Academy of Excellence.

Roof replacement, additions, electrical, plumbing and heating work all need a Jasper County building permit, so ask whether past work on your house was permitted. The Planning and Building office is at 358 Third Avenue, Room 202, phone (843) 717-3650. Reports of code violations go to (843) 547-8290.

  • Plat: $25.
  • Release, satisfaction or discharge: $10.
  • Easement: $25 plus stamps.

Greenwood County was formed in 1897 from parts of Abbeville and Edgefield counties, both once part of the Ninety-Six District. It was named for its seat, and the town took its name around 1824 from a cotton plantation owned by John McGehee.

Lake Greenwood was created by the Buzzard's Roost Dam on the Saluda River, which the county page describes as the largest New Deal project in the area. The county later sold the hydroelectric plant to Duke Power Company.

The lake offers recreation for residents and visitors, and many owners near it hold second homes rather than primary residences.

Who qualifies for the homestead exemption and the school-tax credit?

An owner who is 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind can apply for the homestead exemption, provided they hold fee simple title or a life estate in the primary residence. The Auditor says qualifying legal residents get a 4 percent homeowners credit on school operating taxes and pay only school bond taxes. That credit does not reach second homes, land or business property.

Anyone who sells or rents the home, or changes the owners on the deed, must tell the Auditor. A sale therefore ends the exemption for the seller, and the buyer must apply for their own.

If your notice raised value by $1,000 or more, you have 90 days from mailing to object in writing under S.C. Code 12-60-2510. Send the objection to the Assessor at Room 109.

Agricultural-use land needs at least 5 acres in timber or 10 acres in crops, including pasture. If the use changes, up to five years of taxes can become due, which is a real concern for a seller who is subdividing a family tract.

You have 90 days from the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more. The objection goes in writing to the Assessor.

Employers named include the U.S. Department of Justice, Food Lion, Tupperware and Williamsburg Technical College. The county economic development page adds that Interstates 20, 26 and 95 give access to larger southeastern cities, and that much of the state's population is within about an hour and a half.

Which Williamsburg County offices handle property tax?

Four offices touch your tax bill: the assessor sets the value, the auditor applies the millage, the treasurer collects, and the delinquent tax office takes over after March 16. The South Carolina Association of Counties directory lists the contacts below (directory).

OfficePhoneMailing address
Assessor(843) 355-9321, ext. 5500PO Box 330, Kingstree, SC 29556
Auditor(843) 355-9321, ext. 5600PO Box 7, Kingstree, SC 29556
Treasurer(843) 355-9321, ext. 5900PO Box 150, Kingstree, SC 29556
Delinquent tax collector(843) 355-9321, ext. 5800PO Box 477, Kingstree, SC 29556

The treasurer and the delinquent tax office both list 201 W Main Street, Kingstree, as their physical address, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. except holidays (treasurer page). The delinquent office says it does not take American Express or Discover and does not accept payment on bills that are not yet delinquent.

We could not open a county page for the Register of Deeds, so we are not listing a phone or address for it. Ask the treasurer's office or your closing attorney where deeds are recorded.

When is Williamsburg County property tax due, and what does a late bill cost?

Real property tax is payable until January 15 without penalty, and the first penalty is 3 percent after that date. The county treasurer page and the state code describe the same ladder, with one difference in how the last step is worded.

  • Through January 15: no penalty.
  • After January 15: a 3 percent penalty.
  • February 2 through March 16: an added 7 percent penalty.
  • March 17: unpaid real property, mobile home and similar bills go into execution at the delinquent tax collector's office.

The state statute, S.C. Code 12-45-180, also lists a further 5 percent penalty if tax is still unpaid as of March 17. The county page we opened did not mention it, so ask the delinquent office for a payoff figure that includes every penalty and cost before you rely on any number.

Under the statute, the 3 percent step starts on the later of January 16 or thirty days after tax notices are mailed (S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 45). That matters in a year when notices go out late.

How is a Williamsburg County house assessed, and how do you appeal?

South Carolina taxes an owner-occupied legal residence on 4 percent of fair market value and most other real property on 6 percent (S.C. Code 12-43-220). A rental house or a vacant lot is normally in the 6 percent group, so an heir who inherits a house and moves out may see the bill rise.

Counties reappraise on a five-year cycle, and a county may delay the new values by one tax year by ordinance. An owner must be told of a change of $1,000 or more. The county site posts a homestead exemption application, though we could not open the exemptions page, so ask the auditor which exemptions you qualify for.

The appeal path in Chapter 60 has several short clocks:

  • 90 days from the date the assessor mails the notice to file a written objection.
  • 30 days after the assessor's conference to file a written protest.
  • 30 days after the assessor's response to appeal to the county board of assessment appeals.
  • 30 days after the board's written decision to ask the Administrative Law Court for a hearing.

The statute text is at Chapter 60. In a year with no assessment notice, an owner can still object in writing, and an objection filed before the first penalty date applies to that year.

What happens if Williamsburg County property tax stays unpaid?

Unpaid tax leads to a delinquent notice, a levy by certified mail and a newspaper-advertised tax sale, but the owner keeps the right to redeem for twelve months after the sale. The steps come from S.C. Code Chapter 51 (text here).

  • On or about April 1, the officer mails a delinquent notice to the taxpayer and any grantee of record.
  • If the tax is still unpaid 30 days later, the officer takes possession of real property by certified mail.
  • The property is advertised as a Delinquent Tax Sale once a week for three weeks.
  • After a sale, the owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within twelve months.
  • Redemption interest is a share of the bid: 3 percent in the first three months, then 6, 9 and 12 percent in later quarters.
  • The collector must send a certified notice 20 to 45 days before the redemption period ends.

The Williamsburg County delinquent tax page does not post sale dates or fee amounts in the text we could read, so call ext. 5800 for the current schedule.

What does a deed transfer cost in South Carolina?

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value or fraction of it, and the seller is generally the party liable (S.C. Code Chapter 24). Of that amount, $1.30 goes to the state and $0.55 to the county.

The clerk or register of deeds must also receive an affidavit stating the value of the property, or the reason a deed is exempt. Transfers of $100 or less and deeds in lieu of foreclosure are among the listed exemptions. A false affidavit is a misdemeanor.

How do storms and the Black River affect a Williamsburg County house?

Low ground near the Black River can take on water in a major storm, and sellers should check the flood zone before listing. The river runs about 150 miles through Williamsburg, Clarendon, Sumter and Georgetown counties, and a 75-mile stretch joined the state Scenic River Program in 2001.

During Hurricane Matthew in October 2016, the National Weather Service reported storm-total rain in Williamsburg County approaching 10 inches by the morning of October 8, and a gauge northwest of Kingstree recorded 13.70 inches (NWS Wilmington).

A house with storm damage can be hard to finance with a standard loan, so a cash purchase as-is is one route for owners who cannot fund repairs.

What can you do if you want to sell a Williamsburg County house with tax due?

You can sell before a tax sale and have the unpaid tax paid from the sale proceeds at closing. The closing attorney requests a payoff from the treasurer or delinquent office and subtracts it from your proceeds.

  • Get a written payoff that includes penalties and costs, and ask how long it stays valid.
  • If the house was inherited, gather the death certificate and any probate papers.
  • Tell the buyer about any mobile home on the land, since mobile home tax is billed on the same ladder.
  • If a tax sale has already happened, count the twelve-month redemption window from the sale date.

This page is general information. The offices above set the actual amounts, and a South Carolina attorney can advise on your title.

More questions about Williamsburg County, SC Property Tax Guide

What is the Williamsburg County property tax due date?

Real property tax in Williamsburg County is due on or before January 15 without penalty. A 3 percent penalty applies after that date, and a further 7 percent applies from February 2 through March 16, per the county treasurer page.

Who do I call about Williamsburg County property tax?

Call the county switchboard at (843) 355-9321 and use extension 5900 for the treasurer, 5600 for the auditor, 5500 for the assessor or 5800 for the delinquent tax collector. These numbers come from the South Carolina Association of Counties directory.

How long do I have to appeal a Williamsburg County assessment?

You have 90 days from the date the assessor mails the notice to file a written objection. After that, shorter 30 day deadlines apply at each later stage under S.C. Code Chapter 60.

Can I sell my Williamsburg County house if the tax is delinquent?

Yes, you can sell, and the unpaid tax is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the delinquent tax office for a written payoff first so the number includes penalties and costs.

Can I get my house back after a Williamsburg County tax sale?

Yes, for a limited time. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem real property within twelve months of the sale by paying the bid plus interest of 3, 6, 9 or 12 percent depending on the quarter.

Where is Union County, South Carolina?

Union County covers about 515 square miles in the upstate and is bordered by Cherokee, York, Chester, Fairfield, Newberry, Laurens and Spartanburg counties. Part of the Sumter National Forest lies inside it, and the Tyger River and Fairforest Creek are its major waterways (Wikipedia).

The county seat and largest community is the city of Union. U.S. 176 runs through the county, the Furman Fendley Highway is a four-lane connector to Spartanburg that began construction in 1984, and S.C. Highway 18 links Union and Jonesville.

How did Union County begin?

The county was created in 1785 and named for the old Union Church, a shared log meetinghouse. Scots-Irish Presbyterian settlers had arrived in the mid-1700s near Fairforest Creek, and the county was divided between Loyalists and Patriots during the Revolution, with at least five battles fought in or near it, including Musgrove Mill, Fishdam Ford and Blackstock's Farm.

The old court town of Pinckneyville faded into a ghost town after its district was abolished in 1799. In 1897 the Draytonville and Gowdeysville townships were transferred to Cherokee County. In the 1930s the federal government bought poor-quality farmland, which became part of the Sumter National Forest.

An owner with very old family paper should ask a title company early whether the records sit where they expect.

What is the economy like in Union County?

Health care and social assistance is now the largest employment sector, at about 21.7% in the third quarter of 2023. County gross domestic product for 2022 was about $822.7 million.

Major employers include Milliken & Company, Sonoco, Walmart, Timken, Dollar General and the University of South Carolina Union. Textiles dominated the economy for much of the county's history, and the industry largely closed or moved overseas from the 1980s into the 1990s.

The city of Union counted 8,174 residents in 2020, down from a peak of 10,775 in 1970. Its median age is 42.0. Public schools are run by Union County Schools, and USC Union, a satellite campus, was founded in 1965.

What should a seller know about Union's older neighborhoods?

Union has several historic districts listed on the National Register: the East Main Street-Douglass Heights Historic District, the South Street-South Church Street Historic District and the Union Downtown Historic District. If your house is inside one, ask the county about any local rules before exterior work.

Union has a humid subtropical climate. The Santuck weather station shows normal annual precipitation of about 44.6 inches and about 3 inches of snow, and the city's record high is 110 degrees with a record low of minus 11.

The Delinquent Tax Office is at the same street address and opens at 8:30 a.m. The main courthouse is at 210 W. Main Street. Manufacturing, railroad and utility property is valued by the SC Department of Revenue, not the county Assessor.

What did the 2025 reappraisal change in Union County?

The 2025 countywide reappraisal set an appraisal date of December 31, 2024, and the 2024 taxable value stays the same for the next four years, subject to listed exceptions. South Carolina law requires reappraisal every five years.

  • The notice of valuation and classification is not a tax bill.
  • The county must notify you of any change in value or classification of $1,000 or more.
  • Mill levies are set each year, so your bill can change even when the assessed value does not.
  • Not receiving a tax notice does not affect the validity of the tax, penalty, interest, due date or tax lien.

Keep your mailing address current with the Assessor in writing. Agricultural land that changes use is subject to rollback taxes for the current year and the three preceding years.

How do you appeal a Union County assessment?

File an appeal within 90 days of the notice date to keep all of your options. Instructions are on the back of the valuation notice and on the Assessor's website.

An informal appeal form is available on the Assessor's page. The County Board of Assessment Appeals, appointed by County Council, holds conferences on classification and real property assessment and does not set values or taxes. Either the owner or the Assessor may contest its decision before the Administrative Law Judge Division, and either party may then appeal to the S.C. Supreme Court.

An appeal does not extend the payment deadline. Pay on time to avoid penalties and interest.

When is Union County property tax due?

Taxes are billed one year in arrears, notices go out each October and payment is due by January 15 without penalty. The Delinquent Tax Office page gives the schedule.

Taxes go delinquent on March 17, or the next business day. The county accepts cash, cashier's checks, postal money orders, certified checks and Visa or Mastercard in person, and also takes payment by mail, by phone and through a lockbox. It does not accept partial payments on delinquent bills because its system is not set up for them.

State law (S.C. Code 12-45-180) sets the same step-by-step penalty and gives the treasurer authority to waive penalties on clear and convincing evidence of timely payment.

What happens at the Union County tax sale?

Unpaid properties are sold at public sale, and a person who wants one must bid, because paying the taxes afterward does not transfer it. The annual sale was scheduled for November 10, 2026 at the Union County Elections Office, 1246 S Duncan By-Pass, with pre-registration from October 1. That date has passed as of this update, so call the Delinquent Tax Office at (864) 429-1617 for the result and any follow-up.

  • Delinquent properties are advertised in the Union County News for three consecutive weeks before the sale.
  • Properties that do not sell go to the Union County Forfeited Land Commission and are assigned first come, first served, in cash.
  • A property sold at tax sale can be redeemed with taxes, assessments, penalties and costs plus 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% interest.

The state code (12-51-90) sets a 12-month redemption window, and the county page does not state the length, so confirm it with the office.

  • Confirm the tax map number and the owner of record before closing.
  • If the notice went to a prior owner, ask about a waiver under state law.
  • Get a title search if the land is old family property.
